reply_text:
I read this as **borderline**: it passes all four parts, but only as coverage, and it may be a repeat of a claim already on file.

**1. Are the words on the page?** Yes, exactly as quoted. The Semafor Tech newsletter of 13 March 2024 contains: "Legg told me he came to believe in 2001 that we would have a 50/50 chance of reaching AGI by 2028. He says that number is still about right." The page is a news report: the reporter, Reed Albergotti, writes it up in his own words after interviewing Legg at SXSW "on Monday" (11 March 2024). There's no direct quote from Legg in it and no transcript, so it can only enter as coverage. I didn't open the AI Business link because the search run cited it only as backup.

**2. The admission rule**
- **Part 1 (role):** Semafor calls him "co-founder and chief AGI scientist at Google DeepMind" at the time. That fits "that company's named chief scientist speaking for it." His 2022, 2023 and 2025 claims are already recorded, so the ledger evidently accepts this role.
- **Part 2 (forward-looking, about AI):** It is. AGI arriving by 2028 is about AI and not hypothetical. It states a chance, so it would carry `has_probability`. "AGI" isn't defined on the page, so its test would probably be `unfalsifiable` when entered. Neither point keeps it out.
- **Part 3 (date):** It is dated: "by 2028."
- **Part 4 (source):** It fails as a primary source because Semafor only reports it. It passes as coverage, entered with no quote.

**Why I'm not calling it a plain pass:** the article itself says Legg is standing by a forecast he has held since 2001, and that "that number is still about right." Under the Restatements rule, the same prediction with the same due year is one claim with this date added to `repeated_on`, not a new record. The file `2010-12-10-legg-human-level-agi-mean-2028.toml` has the same year, 2028, but records a mean rather than a 50/50 point. It may be the record that this repeats, or the 50/50-by-2028 version of the forecast may never have been entered. Also, the 2011 files have only the 10% and 90% points, which suggests the 50% point was folded into the 2010 file. The checker should open that file. If its prediction is in effect "AGI by 2028" and it lists later repeats, the answer is "recorded", with 2024-03-11 added to `repeated_on`. If not, it's "pass, coverage only."
